restoration_note: Teaching describes the three permanent works at the consummation: the new luminous land, the binding of darkness's fire, and the sealing of sinners in the last bolos. The fixed-state doctrine controls vocabulary: forever-and-ever doxology, mutual exclusion of Light and Enemy, the prison/wall imagery. Standard formulaic restorations confirmed at gaps {0}-{4}, {13}-{15}, {17}, {19}-{21}. Editor's ⲁⲭⲱϩ at {8} corrected to ⲁⲭⲱϥ on the parallel of the earlier ⲕⲁⲧϩ ⲁⲭⲙ̄-construction. Editor's ⲕⲉⲕ at {18} corrected to ⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛ: the spiritual reading explicitly states the great guard separates Light from Enemy, and ⲡⲭⲁⲭⲉ already follows in the next clause, so the missing pole must be Light. The damaged second-work section ({5}-{7}, {9}-{12}, {16}) provides too few constraints — verbs of binding/quenching could fit but cannot be fixed without more trace.

restorations.basis: Standard Coptic existential idiom ⲙⲛⲧⲉⲩ ... ⲙ̄ⲙⲉⲩ 'they have not'; editor restoration confirmed by the visible ⲙ̄ⲙ- trace.
Future-III prefix ⲉⲩⲁ- continues the modal frame 'they shall...'; editor restoration grammatically required.
Standard idiom ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧϩ ⲟⲩⲃⲉ 'stand fast against'; the visible ⲟⲩⲃ- demands ⲟⲩⲃⲉ.
Greek loanword πέρας 'end'; the parallel formula 'no beginning... no end' from the reading; visible ⲡⲉⲣ- confirms.
Demonstrative copula ⲡⲉ at line edge introducing apposition; standard Coptic syntax.
Lacuna of ~5 chars after partial ⲛⲉⲥ; insufficient parallel or formula constrains the verb/noun. Could fit several plausible items in the appointment-of-the-new-land sequence.
Lacuna of ~4 chars after partial ⲛⲟ; could be ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ, ⲛⲟⲩⲣⲉ, or other; correspondential reading does not fix the term.
3-char lacuna with no diacritical traces; could be subject pronoun, particle, or short verb. The English 'yonder ___ turned upon' allows multiple fills.

Parallel construction with line 11 ⲕⲁⲧϩ ⲁⲭⲙ̄ ⲡⲓⲕⲁⲍ ('turned upon this land') here demands ⲕⲁⲧϩ ⲁⲭⲱϥ ('turned upon him' — the soul/Old Man pressed by the alien body). Corrects editor's tentative ⲁⲭⲱϩ which has no clear lexical fit; ⲁⲭⲱϥ is the standard 3msg prepositional pronoun matching the discussed sense of an alien body turned 'upon him'.
Verb of the second eternal work (binding/quenching the fire of darkness). Plausible fills include ⲙⲟⲩⲣ ('bind'), ⲱⲃϣ̄/ⲱⲧϣ̄ ('quench'), but no trace constrains the choice.
Second coordinated verb after partial ⲛⲥⲉⲥ-; could be ⲥⲱⲧϥ̄, ⲥⲁⲣⲱⲣ̄, ⲥⲱⲣⲙ̄, etc. No constraint to choose.
Single-character lacuna with no anchoring context; could be a particle, conjunction, or article. Cannot be constrained.
Large 17-char lacuna with only fragmentary 'ⲧ . .' trace; the second-work passage is too damaged for reconstructing a continuous clause.

Verb-of-separation idiom: the sinners 'divided themselves one from another' per the reading; ⲁⲩϣⲱⲡ/ϣⲱⲣⲡ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the expected pattern with following ⲁⲭⲱⲩ ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ 'one from another'. Editor's ⲁⲃⲁⲗ confirmed.

Reflexive ⲍⲱⲱⲩ on the next line requires a verb of binding/setting; ⲙⲟⲩⲣ ⲍⲱⲱⲩ 'bind themselves' fits the reading's 'bound together with those creatures in the last bond forever' (lexicon ⲙⲟⲩⲣ = bind, fix in bondage).
ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲕⲁⲁⲩ 'they shall set/leave them' — standard Coptic ⲕⲁ + 3pl object suffix; consistent with the reading's image of sinners being permanently set in the bolos.

5-char lacuna at end of the descriptive triad 'ember-pit / gloom / shadow without number'; could be a fourth comparative or transitional phrase, but the next clause 'which is the prison of the Enemy' does not require it. No trace constrains.

Lyc. ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲉ = Sah. ⲱⲛⲉ 'stone'; visible ⲛⲉ-ending fits. The bolos as 'set being a stone' corresponds to the lexicon's stone = confirmed truth in ultimates / immutable foundation, here as the fixed boundary-marker between Light and Darkness.

Correction of editor's ⲕⲉⲕ ('Darkness'). The reading explicitly identifies the great guard as the wall 'between the Light and the Enemy', and the next line begins ⲁⲡⲭⲁⲭⲉ ('and the Enemy'), so the missing first pole of the pair must be ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'the Light'. ⲕⲉⲕ would be redundant with ⲡⲭⲁⲭⲉ and contradicts the consummation-doctrine of fixed separation between the two essences.
ⲛⲟⲩⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ — negative subjunctive of ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'hear'. The reading specifies 'neither hear one another's voice'; the visible ⲛⲟⲩ- and -ⲱⲧⲙ uniquely fix ⲥ.
Doxological formula ⲱⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ 'unto eternity of eternities'; visible -ⲍⲉ̄ confirms.
Completes the doxological pair ⲱⲁ ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ 'forever and ever'; visible ⲛ-...-ⲛⲏⲍⲉ̄ uniquely fixes ⲛⲁ.
